action: General advice: Chase customers can check that November 16 transfers and Zelle payments went through once; Chase said customers still had access to their accounts and funds. See the separate JPMorgan vendor event.
exec: Chase's outage cause is a software bug per Chase; a separate vendor breach it disclosed on 19 November is, per Chase, unconnected to it.
impact: Thousands of customers reported trouble accessing online accounts on November 16 (6abc); no exact count is given by the sources read.
plain: Chase customers had trouble with online banking and transactions on November 16. Chase said a software bug caused it. Days later it disclosed a separate attack on its vendors and said it was not connected.
date_note: The Next Web, published 16 November, reports Chase's 16 November post about the disruption that day.
summary: Chase customers had trouble with online banking and transactions on November 16; Zelle said an issue at financial institutions may affect Zelle payments. Chase said it was a software bug in on-premise hardware, with no evidence it was cyber-related; the FBI told NewsNation it saw no signs of malicious activity. On November 19 Chase said vendors were hit by a cyber attack, unconnected to the disruption, despite KTEN's headline.
title: JPMorgan Chase outage delays payments; Chase said software bug, later vendor breach unconnected

validation.note: Compared 6abc live blog and Yahoo News (FBI via NewsNation): both give Chase software bug, not cyber-related; FBI no malicious activity. Dropped GuruFocus (403) and removed unsupported Wells Fargo/Bank of America system statements and the 4,700 count, which no page read supports. Beinsure returned 521. 2026-11-20: KTEN (single publisher) reports Chase now says third-party providers were targeted, retracting the 'no evidence' statement; it does not say how the vendor attack relates to the outage, which stays unproven. 2026-11-21: read KTEN and TNW; Chase's 19 Nov X post (quoted by KTEN) says the vendor attack has 'no connection' to the earlier disruption and does not retract the software-bug statement; KTEN's headline and lede say Chase blames a cyberattack, which its own quote does not.

review.note: severity (outage, not attack, thousands of reports: 3 to 2); action advice unsourced (marked General advice); occurred_at 2pm was a Downdetector peak, removed; for-hours and Zelle wording; source published days
